generation.mode: built-in ImageGen edit with edit-target as Image 1 and style canon as reference-only Image 2

lightingIsotropy.metric: 36-bin land-luminance-gradient magnitude peak divided by uniform-bin mean on the delivered source; mask water and its four immediate neighbours are excluded, as are gradients below 12 luminance units.
lightingIsotropy.visualCheck: No whole-cell sun gradient or long cast-shadow field is visible, but basalt columns repeatedly have pale caps over darker side faces and the conifers retain directional light-dark modelling. The aggregate statistic does not establish the literal equal-value rule.

buildableVsSteepFraction.basis: Manual estimated fraction of non-water land area at native source resolution.
buildableVsSteepFraction.method: The broad coherent grassy rock shelf counts as buildable; the narrow broken shoreline rim and exposed stack sides count as steep; talus, shingle, boulders, scrub, and conifer groups make up the remainder. Approximate uncertainty is plus or minus 0.08 per fraction.

south.required: island ground except for the approximately 2 m arriving watercourse at its far end

crown.method: Manual outer-foliage width census of every visually distinguishable conifer crown, including saplings, overlapping-stand crowns, and edge-clipped crowns; native median 29 px scaled by 2560/1254 and converted at 4.8 cm per final pixel.

waterMask.encoding: Opaque white water pixels on fully transparent non-water pixels; binary alpha.
waterMask.componentNote: The large component is the open sea and its full surf and wash. The second is the source-visible short channel/drop, whose painted mouth is separated from the sea by the generated rock rim.
waterMask.method: Flooded source-raster teal and blue from all sea edges, grew through adjacent source-painted pale surf and wash, retained the separate short channel/drop, protected warm dry rock and vegetation, and removed sub-16-pixel water speckles. Dry stacks and skerries remain transparent terrain.

refusalReasons: The island shelf occupies roughly the southern two-thirds of the source instead of continuing only 15-40 m into the 97.6 m cell.
Land reaches 901 pixels of the west edge, which must be entirely sea.
The source paints 244 pixels, about 18.99 m, of sea along the south edge instead of preserving island ground with only the approximately 2 m arriving watercourse at the far end.
The generated short channel meets the sea near the middle of the north rim but does not continue from the required south-edge water arrival.
The overextended shelf remains rich grassy settlement-like ground with extensive conifers instead of transitioning to sparse Shore basalt, talus, and shingle across the south third.
Repeated bright basalt caps over darker side faces and modelled conifer sides violate the literal neutral-lighting rule.
Several shore and offshore columns expose viewer-facing sides and read as regular upright capped cylinders rather than only a thin behind-view rim of weathered broken tops.
More than the allowed one or two close-in offshore stack or skerry groups are present.
openRisks: The water mask follows the raw source rather than repairing its wrong south and west edge topology or its disconnected generated channel.
Buildable and steep fractions and the crown census are manual image measurements rather than surveyed geometry.
No second ImageGen call was made because the returned source was square and the task authorizes a retry only for non-square framing.
Seam continuity and overall visual quality remain director and owner judgments; this report does not claim visual acceptance.
